content: The test image shows a tomato stem with a pronounced tan/bleached canker lesion at a branch junction, with one subsidiary branch completely wilted and desiccated. The affected stem section has a dried, whitish coating. This girdling stem lesion well above soil level suggests Sclerotinia Timber Rot as top candidate.

**Analysis:**

- White/light-colored surface texture on the lesion (consistent with mycelium)
- One branch completely wilted and desiccated (girdling effect)
- Main stem above remains green and healthy
- Lesion located well above soil level

**Comparison with Sclerotinia reference:**
- The reference shows extensive stem collapse with multiple wilted brown stems near plant base
- My test image appears to be an earlier/more localized Sclerotinia stem canker - bleached tan canker with surface mycelium girdling a branch junction
- The bleached tan coloration and girdling pattern align well with Sclerotinia Timber Rot

The localized stem canker with white mycelial surface and branch wilt is characteristic of Sclerotinia. Southern Blight would be at soil level; Alternaria would show darker coloration; bacterial diseases would show vascular discoloration without this bleached canker appearance.
